report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are well-defined and signed off; team has direct stack experience (React, Python/Django, PostgreSQL); however, 3-month deadline with 4-person team and multiple integrations (SSO, PagerDuty, email scheduling) creates scope uncertainty requiring adaptive sprint cycles within predictive phase structure.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to the existing customer analytics dashboard to eliminate manual report generation.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Customer Success Team (15 people) and Sales Team (25 people)
project_understanding.trigger: CSMs currently spend 10 hours/week manually generating reports; leadership mandate to automate dashboards and reduce manual effort.
success_definition: CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes
90% of scheduled reports delivered on time
supporting_quotes: Customer success managers are spending 10 hours/week manually generating reports.
Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to our existing customer analytics dashboard.

assumption_log.what: SSO provider (identity source) is operational, documented, and accessible to development team during build and testing phases.
assumption_log.why: Brief states 'must integrate with existing authentication (SSO)' but does not specify provider identity, sandbox availability, API documentation maturity, or SLA. External authentication is a hard dependency; unavailable or undocumented provider blocks development.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Resource Planning) and Section 12.2 (Manage Communications) — external system availability is a critical assumption for integration projects.
assumption_log.consequence: Development blocked on authentication integration; timeline slip of 2–4 weeks if provider docs are incomplete or sandbox unavailable; potential re-architecture if provider does not support required grant flows.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Proceeding with build on schedule. Risks: If SSO provider is undocumented or sandbox unavailable, team cannot validate integration until late in Phase 2, causing rework and deadline pressure.

assumption_log.what: PagerDuty integration scope is limited to threshold-based alert triggering (UC6, UC7); PagerDuty does not require custom escalation policies, on-call schedule management, or incident lifecycle automation beyond alert receipt.
assumption_log.why: Brief specifies 'Alerting: PagerDuty integration' and UC6/UC7 describe threshold alerts and notifications, but does not detail escalation, incident management, or custom workflow requirements. Scope boundary is ambiguous.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 (Collect Requirements) — integration scope must be explicit to avoid scope creep.
assumption_log.consequence: If PagerDuty integration requires custom incident workflows, escalation policies, or on-call automation, backend development effort increases 40–60%; timeline slip of 1–2 weeks; potential re-architecture of alert configuration UI.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Proceeding with baseline alert integration (threshold → PagerDuty notification). Risks: If stakeholders expect incident lifecycle automation, team discovers scope gap mid-Phase 2, requiring backlog re-prioritization or deadline extension.

assumption_log.what: Email scheduling (UC5) uses internal SMTP or a managed email service (SendGrid, AWS SES) already provisioned and accessible; no new email infrastructure procurement required.
assumption_log.why: Brief specifies 'Email scheduling' and UC5 describes automated report delivery, but does not state whether email service exists, is provisioned, or requires procurement. Email delivery is a hard dependency for success metric '90% of scheduled reports delivered on time'.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Resource Planning) — external service availability must be confirmed before build.
assumption_log.consequence: If email service is not provisioned, team must evaluate, procure, and integrate a new service (1–2 weeks); if existing service has delivery SLA < 99%, success metric '90% on-time delivery' becomes unachievable without re-negotiation or service swap.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Proceeding with email scheduling build on schedule. Risks: If email service is unavailable or has poor SLA, team discovers gap during Phase 2 integration, requiring procurement delay or success metric re-negotiation.

hard.technology_stack: Frontend: React; Backend: Python/Django; Database: PostgreSQL; Alerting: PagerDuty integration

nfr.security: SSO-based authentication required; existing authentication system must be integrated

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Which SSO provider is in use (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, other), and is sandbox/test environment documentation and API access confirmed for the development team?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Authentication integration cannot proceed without provider identity and sandbox access; blocks Phase 2 development start.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is an email service (SMTP, SendGrid, AWS SES, other) already provisioned and accessible, and what is its delivery SLA?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If not provisioned, procurement delay (1–2 weeks) or success metric '90% on-time delivery' becomes unachievable.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: For PagerDuty integration, are custom escalation policies, on-call schedule management, or incident lifecycle automation required, or is the scope limited to threshold-based alert triggering and notification?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Scope ambiguity on PagerDuty integration could add 40–60% backend effort if custom workflows are required; discovered mid-Phase 2 causes rework.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization, sprint planning, and stakeholder feedback during Phase 2–3 sprint cycles?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires active PO engagement; undefined PO role causes decision delays and sprint planning friction.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the current state of the existing customer analytics dashboard (codebase health, test coverage, deployment pipeline), and are there known technical debt or architectural constraints that affect the enhancement scope?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Unknown codebase state could reveal integration complexity or refactoring needs not visible in brief; discovered during Phase 1 could compress Phase 2 timeline.
